text:
support-team: Oakridge just flagged a production regression — p95 gen latency ~3x for our default text-generation route since ~09:10 UTC. Customer reports timeouts on heavy bursts.
elaine: Ack, can you share the exact model + route and a sample request id?
support-team: route: /v1/generate (model: redwood-medium-2025), sample req id: rq_0a9f3b. Seen on both hosted and dedicated edge in us-west.
raj: Thx. Is this across all seq lengths or specific to longctx requests?
support-team: Mostly mid-length (512-1024 tokens) but p50 also up ~30%. Throughput dropped ~40% for the customer.
omar: Can someone grab recent traces & kernel selection logs? I want to see if kernel fallback or quant path changed.
kevin: Pulling traces now. Running: ```bash
./infra/get-traces.sh --customer oakridge --since 2h --format ndjson > /tmp/oak_traces.ndjson
```
sara: FYI support says they didn't change prompt patterns. Could be autoscaler or a batcher regression. Has anyone rolled out the batching heuristic change this morning?
raj: There was a small PR to batching logic merged at 08:45 (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2351) that touched batching timeout. Might correlate.
perf-bot: perf-alert: daily-bench redwood-medium-2025 p95 increased 2.6x at 08:50 UTC (compare baseline run at 07:00). Link: https://perf.redwood.internal/runs/98765
elaine: OK we have a timeline: PR merge 08:45, perf alert 08:50, customer impact 09:10. Let's triage. Raj/Omar, can you run a quick bisect or repro against canary?
omar: Will run a smaller repro locally with stress harness. If it's the batching timeout, lowering it should reduce p95. I'll run two variants: main and revert of #2351. ETA 25m.
kevin: I pushed an emergency canary with batching timeout reverted to canary-rollback-2025-03-17. If customer agrees we can flip traffic.
support-team: Customer is ok with temporary fallback if we confirm. They want a heads-up before config flip.
raj: I'll look at kernel selection logs while Omar repros. If kernel fallback shows extra slow kernels, it could be unrelated.
omar: Quick repro shows latency spike reproduces on canary when using continuous-batching enabled. Attaching small log snippet: ```
[2025-03-17T09:12:03Z] request rq_0a9f3b started, batch_id=1245
[2025-03-17T09:12:03Z] batching_wait=120ms (changed from 32ms)
[2025-03-17T09:12:03Z] selected_kernel=matmul_fallback_slow
```
kevin: That batching_wait looks suspicious — it should be 32ms. PR 2351 seems to have bumped it when burst detection triggers.
sara: If we revert the change for burst detection on the customer's tenant, we should restore throughput. Can we scope the rollback?
elaine: Yes, we can patch a tenant-scoped flag. Kevin, can you apply to oakridge only? If not, flip canary and coordinate with support.
kevin: I can flip a tenant flag without full rollback. Patching now: ``PATCH /admin/tenant/oakridge/config {"batching_timeout_ms":32}``. Will ping when done.
support-team: Please ping before and after. I'll relay to customer and schedule a short maintenance window.
omar: After setting to 32ms, my local repro p95 drops back to baseline.
perf-bot: perf-alert-clear: regression for redwood-medium-2025 resolved in scoped config change.
support-team: Customer confirmed improved behavior after config change. Thanks team :tada:
elaine: Follow-ups: (1) revert PR 2351 or add safer defaults, (2) add a regression unit test for burst detection, (3) postmortem note. Raj owns the follow-ups, Omar will add test.
raj: Taking ownership for the follow-ups. I'll open a follow-up PR and include benchmark results.
kevin: I'll add an ops playbook entry for scoped tenant flags for batching.
sara: Thanks everyone. Closing the loop in support ticket #8942. :thumbsup:
